automataProblem: I created an individual academic project to visualise formal automata and make their simulation accessible through a web application.
automataFeatures: An SVG graph editor for DFA and NFA, textual transition editing, automatic execution, and forward/backward stepping. Models can be saved in browser-local slots or shared as JSON/.fas files. Four interface languages, light/dark themes, and built-in examples support learning. Pushdown automaton and Turing machine editors are experimental extensions.
automataArchitecture: I implemented the SPA in Elm using Model–View–Update. Elm manages graphs, simulation, and hash-based routing; JavaScript connects Elm ports to LocalStorage and file import/export. The application runs entirely in the browser and is deployed on GitHub Pages.
automataLearned: I gained experience with Elm, functional programming, SPA architecture, formal automata and algorithm visualisation.
automataStatus: Completed and defended as my bachelor's thesis at FIIT STU.

trinityFeatures: Live audio streaming from a computer and playback from local MP3/WAV files.
switchFeatures: Learns source MAC addresses, expires stale entries, forwards known unicast frames, and floods unknown destinations. The dashboard shows ports and incoming/outgoing counters for Ethernet II, ARP, IPv4, TCP, UDP, ICMP, and HTTP-labelled traffic, with controls for the switch name, MAC lifetime, and resets.
switchArchitecture: The C# / ASP.NET Core server captures and injects frames through SharpPcap and parses packets with PacketDotNet. The Electron client uses an isolated preload API and main-process HTTP requests to manage ports, the MAC table, counters, and settings.
routerArchitecture: An ASP.NET Core server processes packets with SharpPcap and PacketDotNet and exposes a REST API. The Electron client provides separate route, port, ARP, RIP, and DHCP windows through an isolated preload bridge. Interface addresses belong to the router model rather than changing the host OS.
routerFeatures: Longest-prefix route lookup, recursive next-hop resolution, TTL/checksum updates, and Ethernet forwarding. Management includes connected/static routes, ARP cache and Proxy ARP, RIPv2 timers and interface controls, plus DHCP pools, reservations, and leases.

dndDesc: A local web application for D&D character sheets. Players create and view their characters; administrators manage players and character status. Data is stored in JSON files.
automataLimits: NFA simulation follows a manually chosen path rather than exploring every branch. Input-consuming transitions take priority over λ-transitions; this is not a general ε-closure algorithm. The experimental pushdown and Turing editors need separate evaluation, and saved models remain local to the browser.
trinityArchitecture: The project has separate server and client repositories. The server is written in Rust; the desktop client combines a Svelte interface with Tauri and Rust audio capture, playback, buffering, and networking.
switchLimits: A PSIP semester project at FIIT STU, designed around the original Windows Ethernet lab. State is held in memory, and login is a fixed classroom demonstration without API authorization. HTTP-labelled counters use TCP port numbers. Live forwarding requires compatible adapters and packet-capture support.
routerLimits: Physical routing targets Windows with Npcap and Ethernet adapters. Linux supports API development and hardware-independent tests. Configuration and protocol state are in memory; IPv6 forwarding, NAT, and durable configuration are outside scope. Source and API checks do not establish real-hardware forwarding or protocol interoperability.
dndFeatures: Players create character sheets and track level, attributes, HP, mana, weapons, inventory, spells, and money. Administrators create player accounts, inspect sheets, and manage active, inactive, and deleted characters. The interface is designed for portrait phone screens and supports light/dark appearance.
dndArchitecture: A local Node.js / Express application renders HTML on the server, uses express-session for player/admin sessions, and stores users and characters in JSON files. Portraits are served from local files; devices on the same LAN can use the application through the host computer.
asciiDesc: A Linux command-line ASCII analyzer written in x86-64 assembly for the SPAASM course at FIIT STU.
asciiFeatures: Counts digits, lowercase letters, uppercase letters, and other characters per line and across input files. Supports reverse-order statistics and pagination after every ten lines.
asciiArchitecture: NASM modules compile to ELF64 objects linked with GNU ld. The program uses Linux syscalls without a C runtime, with separate routines for file processing, character classification, string length, and integer formatting.
asciiLimits: Designed for small ASCII files with LF line endings, rather than Unicode text. The assignment specifies limits of 4,096 lines and 4,095 characters per line; these are not a guarantee of robust handling of oversized input.
socketDesc: A C client/server command shell that explores POSIX processes, TCP sockets, and remote program execution for the SPAASM course at FIIT STU.
socketFeatures: Runs external commands and returns their output over TCP, supports file input/output redirection, lists connected clients, and disconnects idle sessions. The client has a configurable prompt; server options control timeouts and logging.
socketArchitecture: The Linux server accepts TCP connections and forks a process for each client. Commands run through fork/exec with pipes and file descriptors; shared memory holds client information, and select handles inactivity timeouts. GCC and Make build the application without third-party libraries.
socketLimits: An educational shell for an isolated lab: connections have no authentication or encryption. The parser does not implement quoting, escaping, pipelines, or shell expansion. Messages use fixed-size buffers and an end marker instead of a general framed protocol.
portfolioDesc: This multilingual personal portfolio: project case studies, work and education details, personal photos, and a downloadable CV in a statically exported Next.js site.
portfolioFeatures: English, Slovak, Russian, and Ukrainian pages; saved language and appearance preferences; system, light, dark, and high-contrast modes. Responsive layouts, keyboard navigation, reduced-motion support, localized metadata, a sitemap, and Playwright accessibility checks complete the site.
portfolioArchitecture: Next.js App Router, React, and strict TypeScript render shared content records through typed translation dictionaries. CSS tokens define layout and themes. GitHub Actions builds a static export for GitHub Pages, including repository-prefix support, with no application backend.
